title: Bollworm (Fruit worm) in outdoor tomatoes - Tanzania

Header: Bollworm (Fruit worm) in outdoor tomatoes - Tanzania
Helicoverpa armigera Funza wa matunda in Swahili

Prevention: Avoid crop rotation with, or nearby planting of peppers, eggplants, cotton, maize, sorghum, cowpea, or okra because bollworms like these crops.
In case of low bollworm populations in the area, grow one or two maize rows around the tomato field, to reduce the pressure of the pest on the tomato.
Monitoring: Bollworms are light /dark grey striped and can be very small (2 mm) when young but grow up to 4 cm.
Search for small young caterpillars on leaves below highest open flowers and on fruit bases.
When the first few <1cm long caterpillars are detected, you may consider action.
Search for small, darkened caterpillar entry holes at the base of the tomato near the fruit stem under base leaves of the old flower.
If you find a darkened hole, open the fruit to search for caterpillar to confirm bollworm.
Fruits with bollworm larvae decay or ripen fast and fruits may fall.
When spotting many holes on fruits, sprays do not help anymore, because caterpillars are already inside.
Direct Control: Handpick small young caterpillar from flower bud tips and fruit bases.
Spray during flowering, when eggs hatch so that new larvae will be killed.
Only the young small <1cm long larvae that are still outside the fruits can be controlled.
Spray in mornings at moist weather.
Spray neem-based products max 3 times (2.5-3 litres/ha or 50-60 ml /20 litres water, or 20-50g neem seed cake or powder per litre water).
Spray reaching coverage of fruits and plants.
Chop 30 to 40 hot peppers or 1/2 litres hot pepper powder into 10 litres warm water (not boiling); Let liquid steep 24h.
Add 10 litres cold water and 20 drops of soap.
Spray reaching coverage of fruits and plants.
Do not spray on ripen fruits.
Remove fruits with feeding holes and also fallen fruits.
Then destroy by chopping, or feeding to animals, or placing in sealed plastic bag in sun.
Restrictions: Apply during flowering, when eggs hatch so that newly hatched larvae are killed.
Only the young small < 1 cm long larvae that are still outside the fruits can be controlled.
Larvae inside fruits are protected from sprays with contact pesticides.
II pesticides registered against bollworm but less toxic alternatives can control the pest.
